idiom_name: free functions generic over trait bounds (impl Trait); a generic service struct only when several operations share the dependencies
implementation_notes: A domain service in Rust is a function in the domain module generic over its ports - pub fn transfer<A: AccountRepository>(accounts: &A, ...) - which gives static dispatch with no vtable and no allocation; traits are the ports and the domain crate owns them, so infrastructure crates implement rather than import. The classic service object is replaced by the function signature itself; when several operations share dependencies or the API wants symmetry, hold them in a generic struct (struct FundsTransfer<A> { accounts: A }) and reserve Box<dyn Trait> for genuinely heterogeneous run-time substitution. Methods stay &self (state lives in the domain objects), and Send + Sync bounds on the ports keep the service shareable across threads.
pitfalls: Generic service types infect every downstream signature (FundsTransfer<PostgresAccounts>); when that leaks through the codebase take &impl Trait at the function boundary instead of storing the type in a struct.
&mut self methods or interior mutability (RefCell, Mutex) on a shared service reintroduce the state the pattern forbids; keep methods &self and let the domain objects own the state.
Async service methods need #[async_trait] or native async fn in traits (Rust 1.75+); boxing every future in a service that should be cheap per call is an easy accidental allocation.
